H1_uniform_amplification.hypothesis: Rain simply raises calling/detection probability uniformly across already available species x stop cells.
evidence: Observed four-component allocation rejects magnitude-matched uniform activation.
Observed allocation also rejects a 75% dry-state persistence-preserving uniform activation null.

H2_weak_call_detection_threshold_only.hypothesis: The apparent recruitment is mainly weak CallingIndex-1 calls crossing the observer detection threshold after rain.
evidence: Full-sample strong 0->CallingIndex 2/3 activation score has positive rainfall slope with 95% CI above zero.
Strong CI2/3 activation contributes ~87.1% of the new-activation rainfall coefficient.
The result persists in same-observer pairs (~86.4% of activation coefficient).
Recorded hearing/noise/wind adjustments and same-observer analyses already retain headline expansion.
H2_weak_call_detection_threshold_only.residual_uncertainty: CallingIndex is ordinal and all unmeasured acoustic detectability cannot be eliminated.

H3_simple_interspecific_social_cue.hypothesis: Rain starts some callers, and route-new species preferentially join stops where a chorus was already present.
evidence: Observed fraction of route-new rainfall slope entering dry-active stops is ~0.519.
This lies inside both uniform and persistence null 95% intervals and is near their means.
H3_simple_interspecific_social_cue.residual_uncertainty: Dry-active status is only a coarse proxy; species-specific or within-night social facilitation remains possible.

H4_simple_new_site_opening.hypothesis: Rain primarily creates new usable wet locations, so route-new species disproportionately enter previously inactive stops.
evidence: Route-new recruitment is not shifted below the null expectation for dry-active allocation.
Taxonomic recruitment excess is much larger than the spatial-axis excess.
H4_simple_new_site_opening.residual_uncertainty: Mapped or survey-night hydrology has not yet been tested directly.

H5_stable_species_rain_trait.hypothesis: Species have transferable rainfall sensitivities that by themselves explain boundary-biased recruitment.
evidence: Route-cross-fit species-specific shift null is rejected in all 4,236 pairs.
Adding strong dry-state persistence remains rejected.
H5_stable_species_rain_trait.caution: An earlier activation-geometry species ranking failed placebo tests and is not a rainfall-specific trait.

H6_stable_physical_stop_rain_trait.hypothesis: Some physical listening stops are consistently more rainfall-responsive than others.
evidence: Temporally cross-fit site shifts have near-zero early/late correlation and ~50.8% sign agreement.
Permuting stop-specific shifts within route does not destroy additive-null fit on the reduced temporal subset.

H7_event_contingent_breeding_activation.hypothesis: Rain-associated conditions move species and local breeding contexts across behavioural/reproductive activation thresholds; the relevant combination varies among events rather than being a fixed species or fixed-site trait.
supporting_evidence: Most new-participation slope is direct CI2/3 activation.
Taxonomic recruitment exceeds spatial recruitment relative to nulls.
Stable species-only and stable-site-only explanations are inadequate in the strongest full-sample comparisons.
Physical stop relocation and simple chorus-attraction allocation do not explain the result.
unresolved_components: Atmospheric cues such as humidity/barometric pressure

H8_universal_threshold_recruitment.hypothesis: Threshold-dominated recruitment after rain is a general rule across frog communities and continents.
evidence_against_overclaim: Strict disjoint-route two-fold NAAMP gate fails narrowly.
AnuraSet INCT20955 does not show threshold dominance.
AnuraSet INCT41 has recent-rain-direction slopes but does not meet threshold-dominance gate.
External effort-complete multi-site matrix replication is still missing.
H8_universal_threshold_recruitment.broader_pattern_still_supported: Rain-associated active-unit taxonomic deepening has cross-dataset consistency in NAAMP and Australian FrogID.

active_next_tests.measured_hydrology: NWI water-regime linkage to physical NAAMP SiteIDs; prefixed eligibility gate and pair-fixed-effect hydroperiod interaction.
active_next_tests.atmospheric_cues: Raw NAAMP schema audit for survey-time/weather fields; only proceed if temporal fields support reproducible ERA5 alignment.
active_next_tests.taxonomic_breadth: Quantify whether strong threshold recruitment is spread across species or driven by a few contributors.
